title: Variational Nonlinearities and Wave Selection at an $O(2)$-Hopf Bifurcation
abstract: At an $O(2)$-equivariant Hopf bifurcation, the real parts $ζ_R$ and $ξ_R$ of the two cubic normal-form coefficients govern selection between traveling and standing waves. In a fourth-order regularized $p$-system, $ξ_R$ was observed to vanish and the cubic nonlinearity to shift only frequencies. We show that both observations are structural: variational nonlinearities enforce them even when the linear part is dissipative and non-Hamiltonian. We consider a class of two-component PDEs on the circle whose quadratic and cubic nonlinearities are generated by reflection-invariant local Hamiltonians of the fields and finitely many of their spatial derivatives, through a common constant-coefficient Poisson operator. Then $ξ_R=0$ for every admissible linear part, while $ζ_R$ depends only on the quadratic nonlinearity. For variational nonlinearities the direct cubic terms are purely imaginary. The mixed cascade term loses its real part because its second harmonic has zero temporal frequency and the resolvent keeps its parity, while the self-cascade at the doubled critical frequency keeps a real part. When $ζ_R\ne0$, the bifurcating traveling waves are saddles, while the standing waves are supercritical and orbitally asymptotically stable for $ζ_R<0$ and subcritical and unstable for $ζ_R>0$. When the nonlinearities are the Poisson operator applied to polynomials in the fields alone, and its symbol does not vanish at the critical and second-harmonic wavenumbers, cancellation for every admissible linear part conversely characterizes variationality. In a dissipatively regularized Boussinesq family, as dissipation tends to zero, $ζ_R$ vanishes linearly off resonance and diverges inversely at the 2:1 resonance. The Hamiltonian limit of the cubic coefficient is therefore singular.
summary: This paper analyzes wave selection at an O(2)-equivariant Hopf bifurcation in nonlinear PDEs. By imposing the condition that the nonlinearities are variational (derived from local Hamiltonians), the authors prove that the selection depends solely on one coefficient, $\zeta_R$. This provides a powerful structural constraint linking Hamiltonian symmetries to the stability of emergent wave patterns.
main_problem: The paper investigates the selection mechanism between traveling and standing waves that occurs at an O(2)-equivariant Hopf bifurcation in nonlinear partial differential equations (PDEs).
main_result: It establishes that for variational nonlinearities, the selection is governed by the sign of $\zeta_R$, predicting stable standing waves for $\zeta_R < 0$ and unstable ones for $\zeta_R > 0$.
method: The analysis uses center-manifold reduction to derive a normal-form system, followed by detailed calculation of the cubic nonlinear coefficients ($\zeta, \xi$) using techniques involving Poisson operators and Hamiltonian structures.
model_or_system: The study focuses on a class of two-component PDEs on the circle whose nonlinearities are generated by reflection-invariant local Hamiltonians via a common constant-coefficient Poisson operator.
key_observables: The real parts of the cubic normal-form coefficients, $\zeta_R$ and $\xi_R$, which determine the stability and selection between wave types.
important_parameters: The bifurcation parameter $\lambda$, the dissipation rate $\epsilon$, and the resonance conditions (e.g., 2:1 resonance).
main_assumptions: The nonlinearities are assumed to be variational, meaning they are derived from a local Hamiltonian structure, which imposes strong constraints on the coefficients ($\xi_R=0$).
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by setting up the problem at the Hopf bifurcation, deriving the reduced normal form via center manifold theory, and then applying the variational constraint to simplify the coefficients and determine the resulting wave selection criteria.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical framework connecting variational principles (Hamiltonian structure) to the selection of stable wave patterns in dissipative, nonlinear PDEs is highly relevant to understanding pattern formation in complex physical systems.
